concerns.text: The plan trains a Bioclim (range‑envelope) model but does not include any assessment of multicollinearity among the 19 Bioclim variables. High collinearity can inflate suitability estimates and undermine construct validity of the niche‑stability metric.

Spatial thinning is applied, yet the plan does not address observer‑effort bias or other sampling biases inherent in GBIF/eBird data. Uncorrected bias may confound model performance and violate the assumption of independent occurrence records.

Power analysis targets Cohen’s h = 0.50 without justification for why this effect size is appropriate for detecting differences in AUC/TSS or delta suitability. An unjustified effect size may result in under‑powered tests, threatening the ability to detect true niche shifts.

The ‘delta_suitability = mean(suitability_2050) – mean(suitability_2005‑2020)’ metric is used as a proxy for niche stability, but mean suitability can change due to shifts in climate variable distributions rather than genuine niche change. This construct may conflate climate‑driven suitability shifts with true niche non‑stationarity.
Plan lists FR‑014 as addressed in the Preprocessing phase, but FR‑014 does not exist in the specification; this is an over‑reach.

The plan states ‘All citations limited to the verified MaxEnt URLs; other datasets are open APIs with no required citation.’ This conflicts with Constitution Principle II, which requires every external citation to be verified. GBIF/eBird and WorldClim URLs are cited without verification, violating the verified‑accuracy requirement.

The plan computes AUC and TSS on recent occurrence records (2005‑2020) but does not specify how absence or background points are generated for these presence‑only data. Without explicit pseudo‑absence/background sampling, AUC/TSS can be inflated and the validation becomes methodologically unsound, potentially leading to a circular assessment where the same occurrence data inform both model fitting and performance estimation.
